CausalChain: Chronic liver injury (e.g., from NAFLD/NASH) -> Upregulation of de novo lipogenesis and suppression of fatty acid oxidation -> Accumulation of saturated fatty acids and C16‐ceramide -> C16‐ceramide stabilizes YAP/TAZ and disrupts p53 regulation -> Enhanced transcription of oncogenic and survival genes, promoting proliferation and immune evasion -> Progression of hepatocellular carcinoma
Hypothesis: In HCC, an imbalance in lipid homeostasis elevates C16‐ceramide levels, which stabilizes YAP/TAZ signaling and suppresses p53 activity, thereby driving tumor proliferation and immune escape; targeting C16‐ceramide’s effects on YAP/TAZ could provide a novel therapeutic avenue for HCC.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is often accompanied by extensive lipid metabolic reprogramming, where increased de novo lipogenesis coexists with impaired fatty acid oxidation. These alterations have been associated with the accumulation of certain lipid species that can function as signaling molecules. Here we propose that an imbalance in hepatic lipid metabolism leads to the accumulation of specific saturated lipid species, such as C16‐ceramide, which in turn stabilizes the YAP/TAZ transcriptional regulators and represses p53‐mediated tumor suppressor pathways. This metabolic shift not only fuels the biosynthetic demands of proliferating tumor cells but also modulates the tumor immune microenvironment, thereby promoting oncogenesis and immune evasion in HCC. Targeting the lipid‐mediated stabilization of YAP/TAZ may therefore represent a novel therapeutic strategy in HCC.
